hints: A request from a city to itself needs no flight, so discard such requests.
Group the remaining requests by connected components when directions are ignored.
A component with no directed cycle can use one directed path; one with a directed cycle can use one directed cycle through all its cities.
analogy: A directed path lets everyone travel forward; closing the path into a loop lets everyone travel in either direction.
example: For requests 1->2, 2->3, 2->4, 3->1 and 3->4, all four cities are connected and there is a directed cycle. Four flights suffice, as in the sample.
algorithm: Discard self-requests. Find weakly connected components of the request graph. For each component with k cities, test for a directed cycle using topological sorting. Add k-1 to the answer if it is acyclic, otherwise add k.
correctness: In an acyclic component, a path through a topological ordering satisfies every request using k-1 edges. A cyclic component is satisfied by a cycle through its k vertices using k edges. Any solution must connect every request component even if it uses extra cities; a nontrivial directed cycle of requests also requires a directed cycle in the flight graph. A connected underlying multigraph containing such a cycle needs at least as many edges as vertices. Combining separate request components cannot lower the sum of these bounds.
